definitions.explanation: Status indicating that a message, email, or document has not been read yet. Common in digital communication contexts.

examples.japanese: {未読|みどく}メッセージが100{件|けん}ある。
{未読|みどく}のままにしておいた。
LINEの{未読|みどく}{無視|むし}は{失礼|しつれい}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think ignoring LINE messages as unread is rude.

notes:
{未読|みどく} means "unread" — not yet read. In modern Japanese, it is used primarily in digital communication contexts.

FORMS:
{未|み} (not yet) + {読|どく} (reading). The prefix {未|み}～ is productive: {未定|みてい} (undecided), {未完成|みかんせい} (incomplete).

DIGITAL USAGE:
- {未読|みどく}メール: unread email
- {未読|みどく}メッセージ: unread message
- {未読|みどく}{通知|つうち}: unread notification
- {未読|みどく}スルー / {未読|みどく}{無視|むし}: deliberately leaving messages unread (socially significant in Japan)

TRADITIONAL USAGE:
- {未読|みどく}{本|ほん}: unread book
- {未読|みどく}の{論文|ろんぶん}: unread paper/article

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {既読|きどく}: already read (opposite) — especially known from LINE's {既読|きどく} notification
- {未読|みどく}: not yet read

CULTURAL NOTE:
On LINE, the {既読|きどく} indicator shows when a message has been read, making {未読|みどく}{無視|むし} (deliberately not opening a message) a recognized social behavior distinct from {既読|きどく}{無視|むし} (reading but not replying).
